newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Liberals score decisive by-election win.
newsitem.headline: Australian Liberals score decisive by-election win.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard's Liberal Party scored a decisive by-election win on Saturday, its popularity apparently undented by a parliamentary row over ministerial ethics.

Election officials said that 80 percent of the vote counted, Liberal candidate Jackie Kelly beat former Labor Party minister Ross Free with over 56.34 percent of votes after sharing out second-preference votes in Sydney's Lindsay constituency.
The result represented a swing for the Liberals of almost five percent on top of an 11.4-percent swing Kelly achieved in the traditionally safe Labor seat at the March general election.

In third place, leading a long list of minor candidates, was the Australians Against Further Immigration party -- which supports maverick MP Pauline Hanson in her campaign to end immigration from Asia. The party won 6.1 percent of votes.
Kelly won the seat in the March election which ended 13 years of Labor Party rule under former prime minister Paul Keating and installed a Liberal-led coalition.
But after a legal challenge by Free, Australia's highest court ruled she had violated the constitution by being a serving member of the air force when electoral nominations closed.
The court ordered the vote to be reheld and Kelly, who is now in the air force reserves, managed to increase her share of the vote in what has been a traditionally safe Labor seat.

The strength of the win will come as a morale booster to Howard's Liberals after a turbulent week in which two junior ministers were forced to resign because their share holdings breached government guidelines.
"This is a tremendous result, it really is," Howard told Liberal Party faithful at a party congress in Tasmania.
Conceding defeat, Free said he had campaigned on such issues as the government's handling of this year's budget, but it had not been possible to dent the government's popularity.
"It was a little too early to recover the seat," he said.
